summary: Replace ShipRight's hand-built sign-in (own JWT, refresh tokens, password reset, Company/User tables, IsAdmin flag) with ASP.NET Core Identity backed by the existing Dapper-style data access (no EF Core), add roles, Google sign-in, and per-company (tenant, CompanyId) scoping of users, logins and roles. Decided: existing accounts and passwords keep working; roles are Admin, Operator and Viewer; desktop/local mode needs no sign-in and must switch over transparently with no loss of data or projects. Still open: how a first-time Google sign-in joins or creates a company.

ask.text: When someone signs in with Google for the first time and has no ShipRight account yet, what should happen?
ask.why: It decides whether Google can create new companies, whether admins must invite people first, and what the tests check for an unknown Google email.

options.label: Only people already in a company (same email) or invited by an Admin can use Google
options.consequence: An unknown Google email is refused with a clear message. An existing account with the same email is linked automatically. Safest: no stray companies appear.

options.label: Anyone can sign in with Google and a new company is created for them as its Admin
options.consequence: Same as today's sign-up, but with Google. Easy to start, but anyone with a Google account can create a company.

options.label: Google sign-in only for existing accounts; no invites, no new companies
options.consequence: Google is just another way to log in for people who already have a password account. Smallest to build, but new teammates must be created another way.

coverage.note: Roles decided (Admin, Operator, Viewer); desktop mode needs no auth; Google first-time sign-in behaviour still to confirm.
Existing User/Company tables (email, PBKDF2 hash, CompanyId, IsAdmin) must stay valid; Google link data depends on the open answer.
Operator vs Viewer rights follow from roles answer; to be written once Google/invite answer is in.
Password and email rules to assume once flows are settled.
Login/signup screens exist; Google button and error states depend on the open answer.
Email is globally unique today (login uses email only); assume this stays unless the Google answer changes it.
Will assume small teams per company and a paged user list.
Removing users and sessions; will assume default.
Email and Google profile data stored; will assume minimal.
Lockout, session lifetime; will assume defaults.
